quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, which of the following do you NOT need to check?

options.text: Fluids.
Headlight and taillight.
Turn signals.
Reflectors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reflectors.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier.
Stopping will take longer.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight means you need more braking force to stop. Stopping takes longer downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight to see better.
Stay very close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible about your lane position and adjust to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Stay flexible with your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Stopping sooner than expected.
Popping a tire.
Taking too long to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, you may lose grip on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic, where should you stay in your lane?

options.text: Stay toward the right side.
Stay toward the left side.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side.
questions.explanation: Stay on the side of your lane away from the parked cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If oncoming traffic is present, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From the motorcycle's previous owner.
From the owner's manual.
From a library book about motorcycles.
From a motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the owner's manual.
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is your best source for information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: On short trips.
On long trips.
After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes occur on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after starting out.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle, how should you apply the brakes?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, either front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle will speed up too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Why should you place a load low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity and hurts balance.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load makes it hard to see over.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity and hurts balance.
questions.explanation: A high load on a motorcycle raises its center of gravity and can make the motorcycle lose its balance.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You use your left foot to shift. Lift the lever with your foot to shift up. Press it down to shift down.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects how you steer.
The front tire powers the bike, so you lose speed.
The flat tire shakes the bike and blocks your mirrors.
You cannot use the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects how you steer.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because it affects your ability to steer. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The horn may go off.
The motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
The motorcycle may jerk and a warning light will turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: If another driver is following too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about it.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Exit the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you at higher speeds.

questions.question: What should a proper lane position do? (Choose the one it should NOT do.)

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other drivers your intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid traffic signals.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids hazards and wind blasts, and keeps others from sharing your lane. It gives you an escape route if a hazard appears. A lane position does not help you avoid traffic signals.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. When is this area unsafe?

options.text: It is never safe for motorcycles.
It is usually safe, unless the road is wet.
It is usually safe, unless it is sunny.
It is always safe no matter the weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in the center lane. This area is usually safe unless the road is wet. The oily strip is often only two feet wide, so you can ride to the side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce the chance of a crash?

options.text: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other drivers closely.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should be visible, signal your moves, keep safe distance from others, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal located?

options.text: On the left handgrip.
On the right handgrip.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest.
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: The greatest risk of conflict between your motorcycle and other vehicles happens at intersections. Stay alert at intersections where another vehicle might cross your path.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Is useless unless done by a mechanic.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should be done only after a ride.
Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could put you in danger.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Always be ready to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: It is important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: You are tired while riding.
You are slowing down where drivers won't expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.
Your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down where drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicle brake lights. Flash your brake light when you slow down unexpectedly, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley. This helps other drivers notice you.
